clickhouse.escape: dashboards over billions of rows read only the needed columns, compressed, instead of whole Postgres rows
clickhouse._why: the 10--100x figure had no source in the row; the speedup depends on query and data; async_insert default changed to on in 26.2 per SettingsChangesHistory.cpp (the analytics child page corrects the docs, which read as opt-in)
clickhouse.consistency: No general transactions: one INSERT into one partition is atomic (all rows or none); multi-statement transactions are experimental, snapshot isolation, not in Cloud. Inserts not fsynced by default; since 26.2 async_insert is on by default (the server buffers small inserts). Replication is async: replicas can be stale.

thanos_mimir._why: timeline label: the dated event is Mimir

iceberg.engine_note: Not a server: Parquet files in object storage, tracked by manifests and a metadata file; a catalog (REST, Glue, Unity, Apache Polaris, top-level since 2026-02-15) holds the pointer
iceberg._why: 1.12.0 is dated 2026-09-29 on the Iceberg releases page (the analytics child page); Apache Polaris graduated to a top-level project on 2026-02-15 (incubator page), as the analytics child page says

duckdb.scaling: Bigger machine only (one process, larger-than-memory spilling); multi-writer via DuckLake (catalog in Postgres or another SQL database; v1.0 production-ready 2026-04-13) or the beta Quack protocol; MotherDuck runs it as a service.
duckdb._why: DuckLake v1.0 was declared production-ready on 2026-04-13 (analytics child page, section 6)

neo4j.reach: Reach for it when the questions are paths and patterns of variable depth (shortest paths, fraud rings, permissions through groups); measured, a shortest path took 5 ms against about 130 ms in Postgres.
neo4j.avoid: Avoid for fixed one to three hop counts such as friends of friends (Postgres joins were faster, measured), for mostly rows and aggregates, or for clustering without Enterprise or AuraDB.
neo4j.escape: path and pattern queries of variable depth that are a page of recursive SQL in Postgres are one short Cypher pattern
neo4j._why: NoSQL in practice measured Neo4j against Postgres on a friends graph: Postgres was fastest for counting up to 3 hops; Neo4j shortestPath 5.0 ms against 129.7 to 138.4 ms for a Postgres recursive query. Graph stores win for paths and patterns, not for counting friends of friends

memgraph.escape: real-time path and pattern queries over a fast-changing graph in memory, where Postgres recursive queries slow down with depth
memgraph._why: graph stores win for paths and patterns of variable depth, not for counting fixed hops (NoSQL in practice, measured)

apache_age.avoid: Avoid when variable-depth path queries are the product (a native store found a shortest path in 5 ms against about 130 ms for Postgres, measured), or on a managed Postgres without it.
apache_age._why: replace the unsourced "much faster" with the NoSQL child page measurement (Neo4j against a Postgres recursive query; AGE plans traversals as Postgres joins)

elasticsearch.escape: Postgres full-text ranks with ts_rank, which is not BM25 (no rarity weight); relevance tuning, facets and log-scale search need an engine.
elasticsearch._why: the Search child page measured ts_rank against BM25 on the same lexemes; the Postgres manual says its ranking uses no global information
